fields.value: Replication Data for: Sodium silicate hydrogels for reducing aquifer permeability: physicochemical, mechanical, and aging characterisation

dsDescriptionValue.value: This dataset contains data obtained during the characterization of sodium silicate gel used as a grouting material to reduce aquifer permeability. It includes both raw and processed data from several experimental analyses. The dataset contains measurements of grout viscosity, density, and surface tension, as well as rheometry data used to monitor the gelation process of the silicate grout. The dataset also includes results from aging experiments performed on silica gels, including syneresis measurements, leachate pH, degradation rates, and the chemical composition of leachate products released during the aging stage. In addition, data obtained from XRD, FTIR, and XRF analyses are provided. Furthermore, the dataset includes PHREEQC input files used for equilibrium and kinetic geochemical modeling, together with the corresponding simulation results. These modeling results were used to evaluate the interaction between silica gel leachate and shallow Dutch groundwater and to assess the potential risk of well clogging caused by precipitation of leachate-derived products. All data are associated with a research paper that provides detailed information on the experimental and modeling methodologies used to generate the dataset.

files.description: This PHREEQC input file contains the kinetic geochemical modeling code used to simulate the time-dependent precipitation of secondary phases during the interaction between silica gel leachates and Dutch shallow groundwater. The model applies kinetic rate expressions to selected precipitation reactions in order to evaluate how secondary minerals may form over time, rather than assuming instantaneous equilibrium. This modeling approach was used to assess the temporal development of clogging-relevant precipitates and to complement the equilibrium precipitation screening.

files.description: This PHREEQC input file contains the equilibrium geochemical modeling code used to evaluate the interaction between silica gel leachates and Dutch shallow groundwater. The file defines the chemical compositions of the groundwater samples and gel leachates, applies selected mixing ratios, and calculates the equilibrium precipitation potential of secondary phases. The model was used as a thermodynamic screening tool to identify possible precipitates that may form when silica grout leachate mixes with groundwater. The calculated outputs include general solution properties and the predicted amounts of precipitated phases relevant to potential well clogging.

files.description: This Excel file contains the complete dataset associated with the study, including experimental results, solution compositions, gel leachate data, groundwater compositions, and PHREEQC modeling outputs. The file is organized into separate sheets corresponding to the different experimental and modeling parts of the study. These data were used to evaluate the chemical evolution of silica gels, the composition of leachates released during gel aging, and the potential interaction of these leachates with Dutch shallow groundwater. The dataset also includes the results used to assess the potential risk of well clogging caused by precipitation of leachate-derived products.
